brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

finish.summary: Built 2x2 compact desk (3 full + 1 half-n base) with drawer, covers, capped faces and locked joints; mount spike at 0,0/0,1/1,0 junction carries small platform. Dressed with keyboard on deck and pen in drawer; checks clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Compact desk unit with drawer and corner spike — I'll build it.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

A spike stands where three bases meet at a corner: place three bases around one junction first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.

events.text: Three bases meet at the spike — now I'll add the drawer base and platform.

outcomes.message: a solid spike cannot carry a platform; only a mount spike can: details.steps fits a mount spike on the same junction, then the platform. The batch was rolled back: details.steps is the batch again with this op changed.
accepted, then undone with the rest of the batch: not on the build

a solid spike cannot carry a platform; only a mount spike can: details.steps fits a mount spike on the same junction, then the platform. The batch was rolled back: details.steps is the batch again with this op changed.

result.rollback: Nothing in this batch is on the build: one op was refused, so every op in it was undone. Fix or drop the refused op and send the batch again (a refusal with details.steps gives the whole batch with it fixed: send those ops as one apply); refs and offers from this batch do not exist.

events.text: Drawer and platform set — now I'll finish the desktop and housekeeping.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.
